item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
595
ABPZ20 KNHC 201145
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on newly formed
Tropical Storm Odalys, located located over a thousand miles
southwest of the southern tip of Baja California.

Southwest of Southwestern Mexico (EP99):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure located about 400 miles south of Manzanillo, Mexico have
continued to become better organized over the past several hours.
Environmental conditions remain conducive for development, and a
tropical depression is likely to form within the next day or so as
the system moves generally northward off the coast of southwestern
Mexico. Interests along the southwestern and west-central coast of
Mexico should monitor the progress of this system. For more
information, including gale warnings, see the High Seas Forecast
issued by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD 15-E):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Tropical
Depression Fifteen-E, located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands, remain limited. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for some development of this system by the middle to latter portion
of this week as it moves westward to west-southwestward, and a
tropical depression could form to the south or southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands once the environment becomes more favorable.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Odalys are issued under WMO
header WTPZ31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP1.
Forecast Advisories on Tropical Storm Odalys are issued under WMO
header WTPZ21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP1.

High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Katz/Pasch

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Odalys (EP1/EP162026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...ODALYS IS GRADUALLY STRENGTHENING... As of 8:00 AM PDT Sun Sep 20 the center of Odalys was located near 11.1, -125.5 with movement WNW at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1003 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 45 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Public Advisory Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 201455
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Odalys Advisory Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
800 AM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026
 
...ODALYS IS GRADUALLY STRENGTHENING...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...11.1N 125.5W
ABOUT 1310 MI...2110 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1003 MB...29.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Odalys was
located near latitude 11.1 North, longitude 125.5 West.  Odalys is
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and a turn 
to the northwest is expected later today.  A turn toward the north 
and northeast with a decrease in forward speed is forecast on 
Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to  near 45 mph (75 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Continued gradual strengthening is expected 
during the next 48 hours, and Odalys is forecast to become a 
hurricane by Monday.

Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1003 mb (29.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 200848
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Odalys Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 AM PDT Sun Sep 20 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that the convective organization of 
Odalys has improved over the past several hours. Deep convection 
continues to develop within a band wrapping around the western and 
southern semicircles, with a recent burst of convection expanding 
over or near the circulation center. The latest subjective Dvorak 
intensity estimate from TAFB is T2.5/35 kt. Given these data and the 
improved satellite presentation, advisories are being initiated on 
newly formed Tropical Storm Odalys, with an initial intensity of 35 
kt.

The initial motion is estimated to be northwestward, or 305/7 kt. 
This general motion is expected to continue during the next day or 
two as a low- to mid-level subtropical ridge remains positioned to 
the north. Thereafter, Odalys is forecast to slow considerably and 
turn sharply eastward by Tuesday, then east-northeastward through 
the latter part of the week in response to a developing weakness in 
the ridge as an upper-level trough deepens over the western United 
States. Although the track guidance remains in decent agreement 
through the first half of the week, increasing cross-track spread 
develops thereafter. This appears to be due, at least in part, to 
differences in how the models handle the evolution of the 
upper-level trough over the western United States and the potential 
influence of another developing tropical cyclone tracking 
west-northwestward offshore of southwestern Mexico. These factors 
lead to lower confidence in the track forecast during the latter 
portion of the forecast period. The NHC track forecast closely 
follows the HCCA and GDMI aids through around day 4, then reflects 
more of a blend of the two thereafter as the spread increases.

Environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual strengthening 
during the next couple of days, with warm sea surface temperatures 
and plenty of deep moisture expected along the forecast track. 
However, modest north-northeasterly vertical wind shear may temper 
the rate of intensification during the next 24 h. Thereafter, the 
rate of strengthening could increase as the shear relaxes and Odalys 
remains in a favorable environment. The NHC forecast has the system 
becoming a hurricane by Monday, with some additional strengthening 
possible through Tuesday. Thereafter, progressively drier mid-level 
air, along with increasing vertical wind shear anticipated later in 
the forecast period, should induce a steady weakening trend. There 
is additional uncertainty in the intensity forecast due to the 
potential influence of another tropical cyclone evolving well to the 
east, which could affect its intensity depending on the eventual 
tracks and proximity of the two systems late in the week. The NHC 
intensity forecast lies near the middle to upper end of the guidance 
envelope through much of the period.
